stimuli.text: Researchers collected data from 600 university students. For each one, they recorded conscientiousness score on a personality inventory and grade point average. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.35.

Researchers investigated whether guided hints help children learn to solve puzzles. They recruited 64 five-year-old children and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition solved practice puzzles with hints from an adult that were gradually reduced. Children in the other condition solved the same practice puzzles alone. The researchers then recorded the number of new puzzles out of ten that each child later solved without help.

Researchers investigated whether a phone conversation reduces what drivers notice. They recruited 64 licensed drivers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a hands-free phone conversation while using a driving simulator. Participants in the other condition used the driving simulator without a phone. The researchers then recorded the number of road signs out of 30 that each participant failed to notice.

Researchers investigated whether an expected reward reduces children's later interest in drawing. They recruited 60 preschool children who enjoyed drawing and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition were promised a certificate for drawing and received it. Children in the other condition drew with no reward mentioned. The researchers then recorded the number of minutes that each child chose to spend drawing during free time one week later.

Researchers investigated whether agreeing to a small request makes people more likely to agree to a large one. They recruited 120 homeowners and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Homeowners in one condition were first asked to sign a road-safety petition and two weeks later were asked to put a large sign in their garden. Homeowners in the other condition were only asked to put the large sign in their garden. The researchers then recorded the percentage of homeowners in each group who agreed to display the sign. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.41.

rows.group: The group that was first asked to sign the petition
The group that was only asked to display the sign

stimuli.text: Researchers collected data from 1,200 teenagers. For each one, they recorded the number of hours of social media use per day and score on a depression questionnaire. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.28.

Researchers investigated whether a new drug reduces anxiety. They recruited 150 adults diagnosed with generalized anxiety disorder and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition took the new drug every day for eight weeks. Participants in the other condition took a placebo pill that looked identical every day for eight weeks. The researchers then recorded each participant's score on a standard anxiety questionnaire after eight weeks.

Researchers investigated whether caffeine improves attention. They recruited 80 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition drank coffee containing 200 milligrams of caffeine. Participants in the other condition drank decaffeinated coffee that tasted the same. The researchers then recorded the number of targets that each participant correctly detected in a ten-minute computer task. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.41.

rows.group: The group that drank caffeinated coffee
The group that drank decaffeinated coffee

stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether keeping a gratitude journal raises well-being. They recruited 110 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition wrote down three things they were grateful for every night for a month. Participants in the other condition wrote down three things they had done every night for a month. The researchers then recorded each participant's rating of life satisfaction on a scale from 1 to 10 at the end of the month.

Researchers investigated whether mindfulness meditation lowers stress. They recruited 84 office workers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition practiced mindfulness meditation for twenty minutes a day for eight weeks. Participants in the other condition listened to an audiobook for twenty minutes a day for eight weeks. The researchers then recorded the level of the stress hormone cortisol in a saliva sample from each participant.
Researchers collected data from 500 adults aged 20 to 80. For each one, they recorded age and score on a timed reasoning test. The correlation between the two measures was r = −0.55.

Researchers investigated whether children imitate aggressive behavior that they observe. They recruited 72 preschool children and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition watched a video of an adult hitting an inflatable doll. Children in the other condition watched a video of an adult playing quietly with other toys. The researchers then recorded the number of times that each child hit the doll during ten minutes of free play.

Researchers investigated whether praise increases hand raising in class. They recruited 50 second-grade students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition were praised by the teacher each time they raised a hand before speaking. Children in the other condition received no special response when they raised a hand. The researchers then recorded the number of times that each child raised a hand during one week.

Researchers investigated whether a night without sleep slows reaction time. They recruited 60 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition stayed awake all night in the laboratory. Participants in the other condition slept for eight hours in the laboratory. The researchers then recorded the average time in milliseconds that each participant took to press a button when a light appeared.

Researchers collected data from 400 high school students. For each one, they recorded the average number of hours slept per night and grade point average. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.45.
Researchers collected data from 450 adults. For each one, they recorded optimism score and the number of days of illness in a year. The correlation between the two measures was r = −0.30.

Researchers investigated whether a smiling expression makes cartoons seem funnier. They recruited 90 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a pen between their teeth, which produces a smile. Participants in the other condition held a pen between their lips, which prevents a smile. The researchers then recorded the rating from 1 to 10 that each participant gave to a set of cartoons. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.41.

rows.group: The group that held the pen between the teeth
The group that held the pen between the lips

stimuli.text:
Read the summary of a hypothetical study, then answer parts A to F.

**Introduction.** Researchers investigated whether spreading study sessions out improves long-term retention. They hypothesized that the study schedule would affect long-term retention.

**Participants.** The sample was 90 high school students, recruited from one city. All participants gave informed consent, were told they could withdraw at any time, and were debriefed afterward. The plan was approved by an institutional review board.

**Method.** The participants were randomly assigned to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition studied a list of 40 words in six ten-minute sessions on six different days. Participants in the other condition studied the same list in a single sixty-minute session. The researchers recorded the number of words out of 40 that each participant recalled on a test one month later.

**Results.** The group that studied in six short sessions: mean words recalled (out of 40) = 27. The group that studied in one long session: mean words recalled (out of 40) = 16. The difference was statistically significant (p = 0.01).

Use the three hypothetical sources to answer the question: **Does sleep improve memory?**

**Source A.** In an experiment, 60 students learned a list of word pairs at 9 p.m. Half were randomly assigned to sleep normally and half to stay awake all night. Twelve hours later, the sleep group recalled a mean of 31 pairs out of 40 and the awake group recalled a mean of 22 (p = 0.01).

**Source B.** Researchers recorded the brain activity of 25 adults in a sleep laboratory after they had learned a maze. The more slow-wave (NREM stage 3) sleep a participant had, the faster that participant completed the maze the next morning (r = +0.55).

**Source C.** A survey of 900 high school students found that those who reported sleeping fewer than six hours on school nights had lower average grades than those who slept eight hours or more. The researchers noted that students who slept less also reported more stress and more hours of paid work.

questions.stem: In the strange situation, a toddler clings to his mother, is extremely upset when she leaves and both seeks and resists her when she returns. Which attachment style is this?

options.why: Separation anxiety is the distress that infants show when a familiar caregiver leaves, which peaks around 13 months.
Secure attachment is the attachment style in which a child uses the caregiver as a safe base, is upset when the caregiver leaves and is comforted on return.
Contact comfort is the comfort from physical touch that Harlow showed is more important to attachment than feeding.
Correct. Anxious attachment is the insecure attachment style in which a child is very upset by separation and is not easily comforted on reunion.

questions.explanation: Anxious attachment is the insecure attachment style in which a child is very upset by separation and is not easily comforted on reunion.

questions.stem: If the data were shown on a scatterplot, what pattern would the points form?

options.text: A loose band that slopes downward from left to right
options.why: That would show a negative correlation.

options.text: A loose band that slopes upward from left to right
options.why: Correct. A moderate positive correlation appears as a band of points sloping upward.
Only a correlation of +1.00 or −1.00 gives a perfect line.

options.text: A shapeless cloud with no slope
options.why: That would show a correlation near zero.

questions.explanation: A moderate positive correlation appears as a band of points sloping upward.

questions.stem: As well as obtaining permission from the parents, the researchers asked each child whether he or she was willing to take part. What is the child's agreement called?

options.why: Confidentiality is keeping data private.
Debriefing happens after the study.
Deception is misleading participants about the study.
Correct. Minors cannot give legal consent, so they give assent and their parents give consent.

questions.explanation: Minors cannot give legal consent, so they give assent and their parents give consent.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the Gestalt principle that we fill in gaps to see a complete, whole object?

options.why: Proximity is the Gestalt principle that we group together objects that are near each other.
Figure and ground is the Gestalt principle that we organize a scene into an object that stands out and its background.
Similarity is the Gestalt principle that we group together objects that look alike.
Correct. Closure is the Gestalt principle that we fill in gaps to see a complete, whole object.

questions.explanation: Closure is the Gestalt principle that we fill in gaps to see a complete, whole object.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes reciprocal determinism?

options.text: The statistical method that finds clusters of related test items, used to identify basic traits
options.why: That describes factor analysis.

options.text: All the thoughts and feelings a person has in answer to the question 'Who am I?'
options.why: That describes self-concept.

options.text: The belief in one's own ability to succeed at a particular task
options.why: That describes self-efficacy.

options.text: The idea that a person's behavior, thoughts and environment all influence one another
options.why: Correct. This is what reciprocal determinism means.

questions.explanation: Reciprocal determinism is the idea that a person's behavior, thoughts and environment all influence one another.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the brief sensory memory of a visual image, which lasts a few tenths of a second?

options.why: Working memory is the active processing of information held in mind, combining new input with knowledge from long-term memory.
Long-term memory is the relatively permanent and limitless store of knowledge, skills and experiences.
Echoic memory is the sensory memory of a sound, which lasts three or four seconds.
Correct. Iconic memory is the brief sensory memory of a visual image, which lasts a few tenths of a second.

questions.explanation: Iconic memory is the brief sensory memory of a visual image, which lasts a few tenths of a second.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes hoarding disorder?

options.text: A repeated action that a person feels driven to perform to reduce anxiety
options.why: That describes a compulsion.

options.text: The disorder in which a person has unwanted repeated thoughts and feels driven to perform repeated actions
options.why: That describes obsessive-compulsive disorder.

options.text: An unwanted thought or urge that keeps returning and causes anxiety
options.why: That describes an obsession.

options.text: The disorder in which a person cannot throw away possessions, so that living spaces become cluttered
options.why: Correct. This is what hoarding disorder means.

questions.explanation: Hoarding disorder is the disorder in which a person cannot throw away possessions, so that living spaces become cluttered.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes egocentrism?

options.text: The understanding that quantity stays the same when shape or arrangement changes
options.why: That describes conservation.

options.text: The understanding that things continue to exist when they are out of sight
options.why: That describes object permanence.

options.text: The difficulty that young children have in taking another person's point of view
options.why: Correct. This is what egocentrism means.

options.text: The understanding that an action can be undone to return things to their original state
options.why: That describes reversibility.

questions.explanation: Egocentrism is the difficulty that young children have in taking another person's point of view.

questions.stem: During deep sleep, the body releases growth hormone and repairs muscle tissue. This best supports which function of sleep?

options.why: Memory consolidation is the strengthening of memories that takes place during sleep.
The activation-synthesis theory is the theory that dreams are the brain's attempt to make sense of random neural activity during sleep.
The consolidation theory is the theory that dreaming helps sort and strengthen the day's memories.
Correct. Restoration is the repair of body and brain tissue that takes place during sleep.

questions.explanation: Restoration is the repair of body and brain tissue that takes place during sleep.

questions.stem: On the way home, Lin remembers that she must stop to buy milk. Which kind of memory is this?

options.why: Procedural memory is the implicit memory of how to perform skills and actions.
Episodic memory is the explicit memory of personally experienced events.
Correct. Prospective memory is the memory to carry out a planned action in the future.
Semantic memory is the explicit memory of facts and general knowledge.

questions.explanation: Prospective memory is the memory to carry out a planned action in the future.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a concept?

options.text: The changing of an existing schema to fit new information
options.why: That describes accommodation.

options.text: The interpretation of a new experience in terms of an existing schema
options.why: That describes assimilation.

options.text: A mental grouping of similar objects, events, ideas or people
options.why: Correct. This is what a concept means.

options.text: The best or most typical example of a category
options.why: That describes a prototype.

questions.explanation: A concept is a mental grouping of similar objects, events, ideas or people.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the Flynn effect?

options.text: The level of performance typical of a certain chronological age on an intelligence test
options.why: That describes mental age.

options.text: The steady rise in average intelligence test scores over the generations
options.why: Correct. This is what the Flynn effect means.

options.text: Originally, mental age divided by chronological age and multiplied by 100
options.why: That describes the intelligence quotient.

options.text: The theory that people have several independent kinds of intelligence, such as musical and interpersonal
options.why: That describes multiple intelligences.

questions.explanation: The Flynn effect is the steady rise in average intelligence test scores over the generations.

questions.stem: Each time Ali finishes his homework, his mother gives him praise, and he does his homework more often. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Negative reinforcement is the strengthening of a behavior by removing an unpleasant stimulus after it.
Negative punishment is the weakening of a behavior by removing a pleasant stimulus after it.
Correct. Positive reinforcement is the strengthening of a behavior by adding a pleasant stimulus after it.
Positive punishment is the weakening of a behavior by adding an unpleasant stimulus after it.

questions.explanation: Positive reinforcement is the strengthening of a behavior by adding a pleasant stimulus after it.

questions.stem: A three-year-old says 'I runned fast' and 'two foots'. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Overgeneralization is the applying of a grammar rule too widely, as in 'goed' or 'mouses'.
Telegraphic speech is the two-word stage in which a child uses mostly nouns and verbs, such as 'want juice'.
Babbling is the stage from about four months in which infants produce many consonant-vowel sounds, such as 'ba-ba'.
Cooing is the vowel-like sounds, such as 'ooh', that infants make from about two months.

questions.explanation: Overgeneralization is the applying of a grammar rule too widely, as in 'goed' or 'mouses'.

questions.stem: Why did the researchers assign the participants to the two conditions at random?

options.text: So that the two groups would be similar at the start, and any difference could be attributed to the independent variable
options.why: Correct. Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

options.text: So that the results could be generalized to the whole population
options.why: That is the purpose of random sampling, not random assignment.

options.text: So that the study would have more participants
options.why: Random assignment does not change the sample size.

options.text: So that nobody would know the hypothesis
options.why: That describes a blind procedure.

questions.explanation: Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

questions.stem: Four studies of child development report these correlation coefficients: −0.61, +0.35, +0.12, −0.20. Which coefficient shows the strongest relationship?

options.why: +0.35 is closer to zero.
+0.12 is closer to zero.
−0.20 is closer to zero.
Correct. Strength is the distance from zero, whatever the sign; −0.61 is farthest from zero.

questions.explanation: The sign of a correlation shows its direction; its distance from zero shows its strength. −0.61 is farthest from zero.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the operational definition of the dependent variable?

options.why: This is the independent variable.
This names the variable but does not say how it was measured.

options.text: The random assignment of each one to a condition
options.why: This is a control procedure, not a definition of a variable.

options.text: The number of minutes that each child chose to spend drawing during free time one week later
options.why: Correct. An operational definition states exactly how a variable is measured.

questions.explanation: An operational definition states exactly how a variable is measured.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a drug, such as alcohol, that slows neural activity and body functions?

options.why: A stimulant is a drug, such as caffeine or cocaine, that speeds up neural activity and body functions.
Correct. A depressant is a drug, such as alcohol, that slows neural activity and body functions.
A hallucinogen is a drug, such as marijuana, that distorts perception and can cause sensory experiences without sensory input.
An opioid is a drug, such as heroin, that relieves pain by acting on endorphin receptors and is highly addictive.

questions.explanation: A depressant is a drug, such as alcohol, that slows neural activity and body functions.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the tendency, after learning an outcome, to believe one would have predicted it?

options.why: Correct. Hindsight bias is the tendency, after learning an outcome, to believe one would have predicted it.
Social desirability bias is the tendency of participants to answer in a way that makes them look good.
Overconfidence is the tendency to be more certain than correct about one's own judgments.
Self-report bias is the inaccuracy that arises when people describe their own behavior or feelings.

questions.explanation: Hindsight bias is the tendency, after learning an outcome, to believe one would have predicted it.

questions.stem: Since his teens, Vic has lied, stolen and hurt people without feeling any guilt or remorse. Which disorder does this suggest?

options.why: Avoidant personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by extreme sensitivity to rejection and avoidance of social contact.
Histrionic personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by excessive emotion and attention seeking.
Borderline personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by unstable moods, relationships and self-image, and by impulsive behavior.
Correct. Antisocial personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by a lack of conscience and disregard for the rights of others.

questions.explanation: Antisocial personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by a lack of conscience and disregard for the rights of others.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant
options.why: A p value of 0.41 is far above 0.05.

options.text: The study shows that the two conditions always give identical results
options.why: A non-significant result does not show that there is no effect at all.

options.text: The difference between the groups is not statistically significant, so it could easily be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

options.text: The independent variable had a large effect
options.why: The averages are close and the difference is not significant.

questions.explanation: A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the tendency to judge other cultures by the standards of one's own culture?

options.why: Correct. Ethnocentrism is the tendency to judge other cultures by the standards of one's own culture.
Prejudice is an unjustified negative attitude toward a group and its members.
The just-world phenomenon is the tendency to believe that people get what they deserve.
Discrimination is unjustified negative behavior toward a group and its members.

questions.explanation: Ethnocentrism is the tendency to judge other cultures by the standards of one's own culture.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the opponent-process theory?

options.text: The ability to respond to visual information without consciously seeing it
options.why: That describes blindsight.

options.text: The theory that color is processed in opposing pairs: red–green, blue–yellow and black–white
options.why: Correct. This is what the opponent-process theory means.

options.text: A form of color vision deficiency in which one of the three types of cones does not work
options.why: That describes dichromatism.

options.text: The inability to recognize faces, even familiar ones, after brain damage
options.why: That describes prosopagnosia.

questions.explanation: The opponent-process theory is the theory that color is processed in opposing pairs: red–green, blue–yellow and black–white.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the group of personality disorders marked by dramatic, emotional or erratic behavior: antisocial, borderline, histrionic and narcissistic?

options.why: Cluster A is the group of personality disorders marked by odd or eccentric behavior: paranoid, schizoid and schizotypal.
Cluster C is the group of personality disorders marked by anxious or fearful behavior: avoidant, dependent and obsessive-compulsive.
A personality disorder is a lasting, rigid pattern of behavior and inner experience that differs from cultural expectations and impairs functioning.
Correct. Cluster B is the group of personality disorders marked by dramatic, emotional or erratic behavior: antisocial, borderline, histrionic and narcissistic.

questions.explanation: Cluster B is the group of personality disorders marked by dramatic, emotional or erratic behavior: antisocial, borderline, histrionic and narcissistic.

questions.stem: In Sam's community, women are expected to care for children and men are expected to earn money. These expectations are examples of which of the following?

options.why: Sexual orientation is the direction of a person's enduring sexual attraction.
Gender is the socially and culturally influenced attitudes, feelings and behaviors that a culture links to being a boy, girl, man or woman.
Sex is the biological characteristics, such as chromosomes and anatomy, by which people are classified as male, female or intersex.
Correct. A gender role is the set of behaviors that a culture expects of men or of women.

questions.explanation: A gender role is the set of behaviors that a culture expects of men or of women.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes shape constancy?

options.text: The perception of motion when a series of still images or lights is shown in quick succession
options.why: That describes apparent movement.

options.text: The perception that an object keeps the same shape even when the viewing angle changes
options.why: Correct. This is what shape constancy means.

options.text: The perception that an object keeps the same size even when its image on the retina changes
options.why: That describes size constancy.

options.text: The perception that an object keeps the same color under different lighting
options.why: That describes color constancy.

questions.explanation: Shape constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same shape even when the viewing angle changes.

questions.stem: If the data were shown on a scatterplot, what pattern would the points form?

options.why: Only a correlation of +1.00 or −1.00 gives a perfect line.

options.text: A loose band that slopes upward from left to right
options.why: Correct. A moderate positive correlation appears as a band of points sloping upward.

options.text: A shapeless cloud with no slope
options.why: That would show a correlation near zero.

options.text: A loose band that slopes downward from left to right
options.why: That would show a negative correlation.

questions.explanation: A moderate positive correlation appears as a band of points sloping upward.

questions.stem: A crawling infant refuses to cross a sheet of glass over what looks like a steep drop. Which apparatus is being used?

options.why: Correct. The visual cliff is the laboratory apparatus with a glass-covered drop that is used to test depth perception in infants.
A teratogen is a harmful agent, such as alcohol or a virus, that can damage an embryo or fetus.
Fine motor skills is the movements that use small muscles, such as grasping a crayon or buttoning a shirt.
The rooting reflex is a newborn's automatic turning of the head toward a touch on the cheek, to find food.

questions.explanation: The visual cliff is the laboratory apparatus with a glass-covered drop that is used to test depth perception in infants.

questions.stem: Which part of a neuron first receives a chemical message from a neighboring neuron?

options.why: The myelin sheath is the fatty layer around some axons that speeds up neural impulses.
The axon terminals is the endings of the axon that release neurotransmitters.
The cell body is the part of the neuron that contains the nucleus and keeps the cell alive.
Correct. A dendrite is a branching extension of a neuron that receives messages from other neurons.

questions.explanation: A dendrite is a branching extension of a neuron that receives messages from other neurons.

questions.stem: A coil held against a patient's scalp sends magnetic pulses into the cortex to relieve depression, with no anesthesia and no seizure. Which treatment is this?

options.why: Correct. Transcranial magnetic stimulation is the treatment in which repeated magnetic pulses are applied to the surface of the brain to treat depression.
Electroconvulsive therapy is the treatment for severe depression in which a brief electric current is passed through the brain of an anesthetized patient.
Psychotropic medication is any drug that acts on the brain to treat the symptoms of a psychological disorder.
A lobotomy is the now-abandoned form of psychosurgery that cut the nerves connecting the frontal lobes to the rest of the brain.

questions.explanation: Transcranial magnetic stimulation is the treatment in which repeated magnetic pulses are applied to the surface of the brain to treat depression.

questions.stem: Immediately after hearing a shopping list, Ken can repeat the final three items but not the middle ones. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: The serial position effect is the tendency to remember the first and last items in a list better than the middle ones.
The primacy effect is the tendency to remember the first items in a list well.
Correct. The recency effect is the tendency to remember the last items in a list well.
The spacing effect is the finding that study spread over time produces better long-term memory than study crammed together.

questions.explanation: The recency effect is the tendency to remember the last items in a list well.

questions.stem: After two neurons fire together repeatedly, the synapse between them becomes more efficient. What is this process called?

options.why: The central executive is the part of working memory that directs attention and coordinates the other parts.
The visuospatial sketchpad is the part of working memory that briefly holds images and spatial information.
Correct. Long-term potentiation is the strengthening of the connections between neurons after repeated activation, which is the biological basis of memory.
The phonological loop is the part of working memory that briefly holds spoken and written words.

questions.explanation: Long-term potentiation is the strengthening of the connections between neurons after repeated activation, which is the biological basis of memory.

questions.stem: A nine-year-old is asked whether she is willing to take part in a study after her parents have given permission. What is her agreement called?

options.why: Debriefing is the explaining of a study's purpose, and any deception, to participants after it ends.
Correct. Informed assent is the agreement of a minor to take part in a study, given in addition to a parent's consent.
Informed consent is the agreement of participants to take part after they have been told what a study involves.
Protection from harm is the requirement that researchers keep the physical and psychological risks to participants as low as possible.

questions.explanation: Informed assent is the agreement of a minor to take part in a study, given in addition to a parent's consent.

questions.stem: After losing a match, Eli thinks, 'It was one bad day and the wind was against me; I will do better next week.' Which explanatory style is this?

options.why: Correct. An optimistic explanatory style is the habit of explaining bad events as temporary, specific and caused by outside factors.
The fundamental attribution error is the tendency, when judging other people's behavior, to overestimate personal traits and underestimate the situation.
A pessimistic explanatory style is the habit of explaining bad events as lasting, affecting everything and caused by oneself.
The self-serving bias is the tendency to credit our successes to ourselves and blame our failures on outside factors.

questions.explanation: An optimistic explanatory style is the habit of explaining bad events as temporary, specific and caused by outside factors.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes REM sleep?

options.text: The brief, light first stage of sleep, in which a person may have hypnagogic sensations such as falling
options.why: That describes NREM stage 1.

options.text: The deep sleep stage marked by slow delta waves, in which a person is hard to wake
options.why: That describes NREM stage 3.

options.text: The sleep stage with rapid eye movements, vivid dreams, an active brain and relaxed muscles
options.why: Correct. This is what REM sleep means.

options.text: The tendency to have more REM sleep after being deprived of it
options.why: That describes REM rebound.

questions.explanation: REM sleep is the sleep stage with rapid eye movements, vivid dreams, an active brain and relaxed muscles.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes nature and nurture?

options.text: Research that follows the same people and retests them over a long period
options.why: That describes a longitudinal study.

options.text: The developmental question of how heredity and experience together shape a person
options.why: Correct. This is what nature and nurture means.

options.text: The view that development happens in distinct stages, like a staircase
options.why: That describes discontinuous development.

options.text: The developmental question of which traits stay the same through life and which ones alter
options.why: That describes stability and change.

questions.explanation: Nature and nurture is the developmental question of how heredity and experience together shape a person.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes extraversion?

options.text: The Big Five trait of being organized, careful and self-disciplined
options.why: That describes conscientiousness.

options.text: The Big Five trait of being sociable, outgoing and energetic
options.why: Correct. This is what extraversion means.

options.text: The Big Five trait of being kind, trusting and cooperative
options.why: That describes agreeableness.

options.text: The Big Five trait of being calm and secure rather than anxious and moody
options.why: That describes emotional stability.

questions.explanation: Extraversion is the Big Five trait of being sociable, outgoing and energetic.

questions.stem: During adolescence, the reproductive organs themselves mature. These organs are examples of which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Primary sex characteristics is the body structures, such as ovaries and testes, that make reproduction possible.
Menopause is the natural end of menstruation and of the ability to reproduce, usually around age 50.
Spermarche is a boy's first ejaculation.
Secondary sex characteristics is the nonreproductive traits of sexual maturity, such as body hair and a deeper voice.

questions.explanation: Primary sex characteristics is the body structures, such as ovaries and testes, that make reproduction possible.

questions.stem: Why did the researchers assign the participants to the two conditions at random?

options.text: So that the results could be generalized to the whole population
options.why: That is the purpose of random sampling, not random assignment.

options.text: So that nobody would know the hypothesis
options.why: That describes a blind procedure.

options.text: So that the two groups would be similar at the start, and any difference could be attributed to the independent variable
options.why: Correct. Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

options.text: So that the study would have more participants
options.why: Random assignment does not change the sample size.

questions.explanation: Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the neurotransmitter that influences movement, attention, and feelings of reward?

options.why: Endorphins is the neurotransmitters that reduce pain and increase pleasure.
Serotonin is the neurotransmitter that affects mood, hunger and sleep.
Correct. Dopamine is the neurotransmitter that influences movement, attention, and feelings of reward.
Substance P is the neurotransmitter that carries pain messages to the brain.

questions.explanation: Dopamine is the neurotransmitter that influences movement, attention, and feelings of reward.

questions.stem: To open a combination lock, Wes tries 000, then 001, then 002, and so on until it opens. Which problem-solving strategy is he using?

options.why: Correct. An algorithm is a step-by-step procedure that guarantees a solution.
A heuristic is a simple thinking shortcut that is fast but can lead to errors.
Executive functions is the mental processes used to plan, organize and carry out goal-directed behavior.
Divergent thinking is thinking that produces many possible answers to a problem.

questions.explanation: An algorithm is a step-by-step procedure that guarantees a solution.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the difference between the highest and lowest scores?

options.why: The standard deviation is the measure of how much scores vary around the mean.
Correct. The range is the difference between the highest and lowest scores.
The median is the middle score when the scores are placed in order.
The mode is the score that occurs most often.

questions.explanation: The range is the difference between the highest and lowest scores.

questions.stem: Lin gives up her seat on the bus to an elderly stranger who can never repay her. Which norm is guiding her?

options.why: Altruism is unselfish concern for the welfare of others.
Burnout is the physical and emotional exhaustion that results from long-term stress at work.
Correct. The social responsibility norm is the expectation that people will help those who need help, even at a cost to themselves.
The social reciprocity norm is the expectation that people will help those who have helped them.

questions.explanation: The social responsibility norm is the expectation that people will help those who need help, even at a cost to themselves.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the disorder in which a person has an intense fear of being judged or embarrassed in social situations?

options.why: Correct. Social anxiety disorder is the disorder in which a person has an intense fear of being judged or embarrassed in social situations.
A specific phobia is the disorder in which a person has an intense, irrational fear of a particular object or situation.
Taijin kyofusho is the culture-bound anxiety syndrome, found mainly in Japan, marked by fear of offending or embarrassing others.
Agoraphobia is the disorder in which a person fears and avoids public places from which escape might be difficult.

questions.explanation: Social anxiety disorder is the disorder in which a person has an intense fear of being judged or embarrassed in social situations.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the lobes behind the forehead, which handle planning, judgment and voluntary movement?

options.why: Correct. The frontal lobes is the lobes behind the forehead, which handle planning, judgment and voluntary movement.
The temporal lobes is the lobes above the ears, which process sound and help recognize language.
The occipital lobes is the lobes at the back of the head, which process visual information.
The motor cortex is the strip at the rear of the frontal lobes that controls voluntary movements.

questions.explanation: The frontal lobes is the lobes behind the forehead, which handle planning, judgment and voluntary movement.

questions.stem: A whisper and a shout at the same pitch differ in loudness. Which property of the sound waves differs?

options.why: Correct. Amplitude is the height of a sound wave, which determines loudness.
Frequency is the number of sound waves per second, which determines pitch.
The cochlea is the coiled, fluid-filled tube in the inner ear where sound waves become neural impulses.
Wavelength is the distance from one wave peak to the next, which determines the hue of light.

questions.explanation: Amplitude is the height of a sound wave, which determines loudness.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The difference between the groups is not statistically significant, so it could easily be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

options.text: The study shows that the two conditions always give identical results
options.why: A non-significant result does not show that there is no effect at all.

options.text: The independent variable had a large effect
options.why: The averages are close and the difference is not significant.

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant
options.why: A p value of 0.41 is far above 0.05.

questions.explanation: A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: In a therapy study, the treated group also happened to exercise more than the untreated group, so exercise might explain their improvement. Exercise is which of the following?

options.why: The control group is the group in an experiment that does not receive the treatment and is used for comparison.
Effect size is the measure of how large the difference or relationship found in a study is.
The placebo effect is an improvement that results from a person's expectation of a treatment rather than from the treatment itself.
Correct. A confounding variable is a factor other than the independent variable that differs between groups and could explain the results.

questions.explanation: A confounding variable is a factor other than the independent variable that differs between groups and could explain the results.

questions.stem: Walking to the phone, Rosa repeats a number again and again so that she does not forget it. Which technique is she using?

options.why: Autobiographical memory is the memory of the events of one's own life.
Correct. Maintenance rehearsal is the repeating of information over and over to keep it in short-term memory.
Highly superior autobiographical memory is the rare ability to recall almost every day of one's life in detail.
Elaborative rehearsal is the linking of new information to existing knowledge and meaning to store it in long-term memory.

questions.explanation: Maintenance rehearsal is the repeating of information over and over to keep it in short-term memory.

questions.stem: Which group served as the control group?

options.why: Only the comparison group is the control group.

options.text: Neither group, because the study had no comparison condition
options.why: The second condition is the comparison.

options.text: The group that wrote about daily events
options.why: Correct. The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

options.text: The group that wrote about gratitude
options.why: This group received the treatment being tested: it is the experimental group.

questions.explanation: The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the way one sense influences another, as when smell affects taste?

options.why: Correct. Sensory interaction is the way one sense influences another, as when smell affects taste.
Synesthesia is the condition in which stimulating one sense produces an experience in another sense.
The absolute threshold is the weakest level of a stimulus that a person can detect half of the time.
Transduction is the conversion of physical energy, such as light or sound, into neural impulses.

questions.explanation: Sensory interaction is the way one sense influences another, as when smell affects taste.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the diathesis-stress model?

options.text: The use of techniques from several types of therapy, depending on the client's problem
options.why: That describes an eclectic approach.

options.text: The view that disorders result from the interaction of biological, psychological and social factors
options.why: That describes the biopsychosocial model.

options.text: The view that a disorder develops when an inherited vulnerability is triggered by stressful experience
options.why: Correct. This is what the diathesis-stress model means.

options.text: The presence of two or more disorders in the same person at the same time
options.why: That describes comorbidity.

questions.explanation: The diathesis-stress model is the view that a disorder develops when an inherited vulnerability is triggered by stressful experience.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the mood-stabilizing drug used to treat bipolar disorder?

options.why: An antipsychotic drug is a drug that reduces hallucinations and delusions by blocking dopamine receptors.
An antidepressant is a drug, such as an SSRI, that treats depression and anxiety by raising the availability of serotonin or norepinephrine.
Correct. Lithium is the mood-stabilizing drug used to treat bipolar disorder.
An antianxiety drug is a drug that reduces tension by depressing central nervous system activity and can be addictive.

questions.explanation: Lithium is the mood-stabilizing drug used to treat bipolar disorder.

questions.stem: All of the subjects in this study were drawn from one group: 84 office workers. What does this most limit?

options.text: Whether a cause-and-effect conclusion can be drawn
options.why: Random assignment, not the sample, allows the causal conclusion.

options.text: Whether the study had a control group
options.why: The study had a comparison condition.

options.text: How far the findings can be generalized to other populations
options.why: Correct. A sample that does not represent the wider population limits generalizability.

options.text: Whether the dependent variable was operationally defined
options.why: The measure was clearly defined.

questions.explanation: A sample that does not represent the wider population limits generalizability.

questions.stem: Which receptor cells let a person see the colors and fine details of a painting in daylight?

options.why: The retina is the light-sensitive inner surface at the back of the eye that contains the receptor cells.
The fovea is the central point of the retina, where cones are packed most densely and vision is sharpest.
Rods is the receptor cells that detect black, white and gray and work in dim light and peripheral vision.
Correct. Cones is the receptor cells that detect color and fine detail and work in bright light.

questions.explanation: Cones is the receptor cells that detect color and fine detail and work in bright light.

questions.stem: Receptors in Tia's fingertip detect a pinprick, and a signal travels toward her spinal cord. Which cells carry this incoming signal?

options.why: The reflex arc is the simple automatic pathway in which the spinal cord produces a response before the brain is aware of the stimulus.
Interneurons is the neurons inside the brain and spinal cord that pass messages between sensory inputs and motor outputs.
Glial cells is the cells that support, nourish, insulate and protect neurons.
Correct. Sensory neurons is the neurons that carry incoming information from the sense receptors to the brain and spinal cord.

questions.explanation: Sensory neurons is the neurons that carry incoming information from the sense receptors to the brain and spinal cord.

questions.stem: Researchers compare how often both identical twins, versus both fraternal twins, develop the same disorder. Which research design is this?

options.why: Correct. A twin study is research that compares identical and fraternal twins to estimate the influence of heredity.
Nurture is the influence of environmental factors, such as upbringing and experience, on behavior and mental processes.
Nature is the influence of inherited genetic factors on behavior and mental processes.
The evolutionary perspective is the approach that explains behavior through natural selection of traits that helped ancestors survive and reproduce.

questions.explanation: A twin study is research that compares identical and fraternal twins to estimate the influence of heredity.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a possible third variable that could explain the correlation?

options.text: The number of years since leaving school
options.why: Correct. A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.
This is the statistic, not a variable.
This is one of the two variables that were measured.

options.text: Score on a timed reasoning test
options.why: This is one of the two variables that were measured.

questions.explanation: A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

questions.stem: Before the study could begin, a committee at the university reviewed the plan to make sure the children would be protected from harm. What is this committee called?

options.why: Correct. An institutional review board must approve research with human participants.
A confederate is someone who secretly works for the researcher.
That is a discussion group used to collect opinions.
That is a comparison condition.

questions.explanation: An institutional review board must approve research with human participants.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as persuasion that works through evidence and logical arguments, which people think about carefully?

options.why: A social norm is a rule for accepted and expected behavior in a group.
Informational social influence is the influence that comes from a person's willingness to accept others' views as evidence about reality.
The foot-in-the-door technique is the strategy of getting agreement to a small request first so that a larger request is more likely to be accepted.
Correct. The central route to persuasion is persuasion that works through evidence and logical arguments, which people think about carefully.

questions.explanation: The central route to persuasion is persuasion that works through evidence and logical arguments, which people think about carefully.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the operational definition of the dependent variable?

options.text: The random assignment of each one to a condition
options.why: This is a control procedure, not a definition of a variable.
This is the independent variable.
This names the variable but does not say how it was measured.

options.text: The number of times that each child raised a hand during one week
options.why: Correct. An operational definition states exactly how a variable is measured.

questions.explanation: An operational definition states exactly how a variable is measured.

questions.stem: A patient stands rigid in one position for several hours and does not respond to anyone. Which symptom is this?

options.why: Disorganized speech is the jumbled, illogical speech, sometimes called word salad, that is a symptom of schizophrenia.
Correct. Catatonia is a disturbance of movement in which a person may remain motionless for hours or move without purpose.
A delusion is a false belief, often of persecution or grandeur, that a person holds despite clear evidence against it.
Flat affect is a lack of emotional expression in the face and voice.

questions.explanation: Catatonia is a disturbance of movement in which a person may remain motionless for hours or move without purpose.

questions.stem: The group that stayed awake responded more slowly. The difference was statistically significant. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: The amount of sleep caused the difference in reaction time
options.why: Correct. With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

options.text: The amount of sleep and reaction time are related, but no cause can be inferred
options.why: That limit applies to correlational studies; this was an experiment.

options.text: The hypothesis has been proved, so the study need not be repeated
options.why: Findings must be replicated; one study does not prove a hypothesis.

options.text: The same result would be found in every group of people or animals
options.why: The sample limits how far the result can be generalized.

questions.explanation: With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

questions.stem: A teacher gives surprise quizzes at unpredictable times, so students study steadily. Which schedule of reinforcement is this?

options.why: A fixed-ratio schedule is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced after a set number of responses.
Correct. A variable-interval schedule is the schedule in which the first response after an unpredictable amount of time is reinforced.
A variable-ratio schedule is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced after an unpredictable number of responses.
Continuous reinforcement is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced every time it occurs.

questions.explanation: A variable-interval schedule is the schedule in which the first response after an unpredictable amount of time is reinforced.

questions.stem: What does the correlation show?

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with higher values of the second
options.why: Correct. A positive correlation means the two measures tend to move in the same direction.

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with lower values of the second
options.why: That would be a negative correlation.

options.text: The first measure causes the second
options.why: A correlation does not show cause and effect.
A correlation of zero would show no relationship.

questions.explanation: A positive correlation means the two measures tend to move in the same direction.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes disinhibition?

options.text: The form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for new experiences through travel, art and unusual lifestyles
options.why: That describes experience seeking.

options.text: The form of sensation seeking that involves a strong dislike of repetition and routine
options.why: That describes boredom susceptibility.

options.text: The form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for risky physical activities
options.why: That describes thrill and adventure seeking.

options.text: The form of sensation seeking that involves a loss of self-restraint, as at wild parties
options.why: Correct. This is what disinhibition means.

questions.explanation: Disinhibition is the form of sensation seeking that involves a loss of self-restraint, as at wild parties.

questions.stem: Which research method did the researchers use?

options.why: Correct. The researchers measured two variables and examined their relationship without manipulating anything.
No variable was manipulated and there was no random assignment.
A case study examines one individual in depth.
A meta-analysis combines the results of many studies.

questions.explanation: The researchers measured two variables and examined their relationship without manipulating anything.

questions.stem: For three years, Otto has felt low and tired on most days, though he still manages to work. Which disorder does this suggest?

options.why: Bipolar I disorder is the disorder in which a person has full manic episodes, usually alternating with depression.
Bipolar II disorder is the disorder in which a person alternates between depression and a milder form of mania called hypomania.
Correct. Persistent depressive disorder is the disorder in which a person has a mildly depressed mood on most days for at least two years.
Mania is a state of extreme energy, overconfidence, racing thoughts and little need for sleep.

questions.explanation: Persistent depressive disorder is the disorder in which a person has a mildly depressed mood on most days for at least two years.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The study shows that the two conditions always give identical results
options.why: A non-significant result does not show that there is no effect at all.

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant
options.why: A p value of 0.41 is far above 0.05.

options.text: The difference between the groups is not statistically significant, so it could easily be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

options.text: The independent variable had a large effect
options.why: The averages are close and the difference is not significant.

questions.explanation: A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: After a head injury, Amir can learn new things but cannot remember anything from the year before the accident. Which condition does he have?

options.why: Correct. Retrograde amnesia is the loss of memories from before an injury or illness.
Anterograde amnesia is the inability to form new memories after an injury or illness.
Alzheimer's disease is a progressive brain disease that destroys memory and then other mental abilities.
Infantile amnesia is the inability of adults to remember events from the first few years of life.

questions.explanation: Retrograde amnesia is the loss of memories from before an injury or illness.

questions.stem: After being shouted at by her boss, Gia goes home and shouts at her younger brother. Which defense mechanism is this?

options.why: Denial is the defense mechanism of refusing to accept a painful reality.
Projection is the defense mechanism of seeing one's own unacceptable impulses in other people.
Rationalization is the defense mechanism of giving a comfortable excuse in place of the real reason for a behavior.
Correct. Displacement is the defense mechanism of shifting an impulse from its real target to a safer one.

questions.explanation: Displacement is the defense mechanism of shifting an impulse from its real target to a safer one.

questions.stem: Railway tracks in a drawing appear to come together at the horizon, which makes the scene look deep. Which depth cue is this?

options.why: Interposition is the monocular depth cue in which an object that partly blocks another is seen as closer.
Relative size is the monocular depth cue in which the object that casts the smaller image is seen as farther away.
Convergence is the binocular depth cue based on how far the eyes turn inward to focus on a near object.
Correct. Linear perspective is the monocular depth cue in which parallel lines seem to meet in the distance.

questions.explanation: Linear perspective is the monocular depth cue in which parallel lines seem to meet in the distance.

questions.stem: An eighty-year-old reflects on her life and feels that it was meaningful and well lived. Which of Erikson's stages is this?

options.why: Identity versus role confusion is Erikson's stage in adolescence, in which teenagers work out who they are.
Intimacy versus isolation is Erikson's stage in young adulthood, in which people seek close, lasting relationships.
Generativity versus stagnation is Erikson's stage in middle adulthood, in which people seek to contribute to the world through family and work.
Correct. Integrity versus despair is Erikson's stage in late adulthood, in which people look back on life with satisfaction or regret.

questions.explanation: Integrity versus despair is Erikson's stage in late adulthood, in which people look back on life with satisfaction or regret.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the category of character strengths that includes forgiveness, humility and self-control?

options.why: Humanity is the category of character strengths that includes love, kindness and social intelligence.
Transcendence is the category of character strengths that includes gratitude, hope, humor and appreciation of beauty.
Justice is the category of character strengths that includes teamwork, fairness and leadership.
Correct. Temperance is the category of character strengths that includes forgiveness, humility and self-control.

questions.explanation: Temperance is the category of character strengths that includes forgiveness, humility and self-control.

questions.stem: Scores on a test are normally distributed with a mean of 70 and a standard deviation of 15. About what percentage of scores are between 55 and 85?

options.why: This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
Correct. About 68% of scores fall within one standard deviation of the mean.

questions.explanation: About 68% of scores fall within one standard deviation of the mean. (55 and 85 are one standard deviation from the mean; 40 and 100 are two.)

questions.title: Article analysis: a study of long-term retention

parts.prompt: Identify the research method used in the study.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the method as an experiment.
rubric.example: The study is an experiment: the researchers manipulated a variable and randomly assigned the subjects to conditions.

parts.prompt: State the operational definition of long-term retention.

rubric.criterion: States how the variable was measured in this study.
rubric.example: Long-term retention was defined as the number of words out of 40 that each participant recalled on a test one month later.

parts.prompt: Describe the meaning of the difference between the two group averages.

rubric.criterion: Accurately describes which group scored higher or lower and what that means for the variable measured.
rubric.example: The group that studied in six short sessions recalled more words. On average, the value was 27 for the group that studied in six short sessions and 16 for the group that studied in one long session, and a p value of 0.01 means a difference this large is unlikely to be due to chance.

parts.prompt: Identify at least one ethical guideline applied by the researchers.

rubric.criterion: Identifies an ethical guideline that the summary shows was followed.
rubric.example: Informed consent: participants agreed to take part after being told about the study. (Also acceptable: debriefing; the right to withdraw; approval by an institutional review board.)

parts.prompt: Explain the extent to which the research findings may or may not be generalizable, using specific and relevant evidence from the study.

rubric.criterion: Explains a limit (or strength) of generalizability with reference to the sample.
rubric.example: The sample was 90 high school students from one city, so the findings may not apply to people of other ages, cultures or backgrounds. Because the sample was not randomly selected from a wider population, it may not be representative.

parts.prompt: Explain how at least one of the research findings supports or refutes the researchers' hypothesis.

rubric.criterion: Uses a specific finding from the study as evidence.
rubric.example: The group that studied in six short sessions recalled more words. (27 compared with 16).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the finding supports the hypothesis, using a psychological concept.
rubric.example: This supports the hypothesis that the study schedule affects long-term retention. Because subjects were randomly assigned, the difference can be attributed to the study schedule. The finding illustrates the spacing effect: distributed practice produces better long-term memory than massed practice.

questions.title: Evidence-based question: Does sleep improve memory?

parts.prompt: Propose a specific and defensible claim, based in psychological science, that responds to the question.

rubric.criterion: States a claim that answers the question and can be supported by the sources.
rubric.example: Sleep improves memory because memories are consolidated during sleep.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using at least one piece of specific and relevant evidence from one of the sources. (ii) Explain how the evidence supports your claim, using a psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding learned in AP Psychology.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from one source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source A, students who slept recalled a mean of 31 of 40 word pairs, compared with 22 for students who stayed awake.

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through memory consolidation: during sleep, the hippocampus and cortex strengthen newly encoded memories, so the sleep group stored the word pairs better. Because the study was an experiment with random assignment, sleep can be said to have caused the difference.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a psychological concept in the explanation.
rubric.example: The concept must be named and applied correctly, as in the model explanation.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using an additional piece of specific and relevant evidence from a different source. (ii) Explain how this evidence supports your claim, using a different psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from a different source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source B, participants who had more slow-wave sleep completed the maze faster the next morning (r = +0.55).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim because NREM stage 3 sleep is linked to strengthening the neural connections formed during learning (long-term potentiation), so more deep sleep goes with better retention of the maze.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a different psychological concept from the one used in part B.
rubric.example: The concept must differ from the one used in part B and be applied correctly.
